$comment: The shipped themes, as data. `scripts/build-tokens.mjs` compiles one stylesheet block per entry and publishes the same list in the token manifest; `src/tokens.themes.test.js` holds every entry to completeness and `src/tokens.contrast.test.js` holds every entry to WCAG AA, or to `minimumContrast` where an entry sets a higher floor. Registration is explicit rather than a glob over `tokens.*.json`, because five things about a theme cannot be inferred from its file: which theme the OS dark preference selects, whether a theme reads as light or dark to native chrome, what contrast it promises, what to call it, and which names it used to have. A theme is added by writing its overlay and adding it here — nothing else, and the gates refuse it if the overlay is incomplete or illegible. `aliases` are those earlier names: the themes were renamed for the time of day they suit (light → midday, dark → evening, midnight → night), and an alias is compiled into the same selector as its theme and accepted wherever a theme is named, so a stored choice, an app's defaultTheme and a data-theme attribute written before the rename keep their palette.

themes.name: midday
themes.label: Midday
themes.description: The default. Carries every token, including the geometry the other themes inherit.

themes.name: twilight
themes.label: Twilight
themes.description: A dimmed violet dark between midday and evening: light text on violet-grey surfaces well above evening's near-black, for a room that is getting dark rather than one that is.

themes.name: evening
themes.label: Evening
themes.description: The slate-neutral dark counterpart to midday.

themes.name: night
themes.label: Night
themes.description: A near-black dark for low light and OLED displays: cooler neutrals, a deeper canvas than evening, and a deeper accent that holds a white label at AA. The theme the OS dark preference selects.

themes.name: contrast
themes.label: High contrast
themes.description: A high-contrast light theme: white surfaces, near-black text, darkened accents and visible borders. Every declared text pairing reaches AAA, not just AA. Not wired to `prefers-contrast: more` — that needs a dark high-contrast counterpart first, or a user who asked for both more contrast and dark would be handed a light theme.
